newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian PM rules out talk of Yeltsin quitting.
newsitem.headline: Russian PM rules out talk of Yeltsin quitting.

text.p: Russia's prime minister on Tuesday ruled out suggestions that President Boris Yeltsin might resign for health reasons and a surgeon denied planned surgery on the president's heart would be cancelled.

Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said calls by the opposition Communist Party for the 65-year-old president to step down if he could not work normally were unacceptable and that there was no question of him quitting.
"This is out of the question now," Interfax news agency quoted Chernomyrdin as saying in reply to a reporter's question about whether the president might resign.
Chernomyrdin had met Yeltsin earlier on Tuesday at Moscow's Central Clinical Hospital where the Kremlin leader is preparing for heart surgery.
A team of doctors, including U.S. specialist Michael DeBakey, is due to meet Yeltsin around noon (0800 GMT) on Wednesday to discuss a possible date for Yeltsin's planned heart bypass operation.
"The council (of doctors) will discuss the date, tactics and the extent of the forthcoming operation," presidential press secretary Sergei Yastrzhembsky told a news briefing.
Cardiac surgeon Renat Akchurin, who is widely expected to be in charge of the operation, said there was no chance of the surgery being cancelled.
Asked by reporters if it was possible that plans for the operation could be scrapped, he replied: "No."

Akchurin, who was speaking during a medical conference in Moscow, had said at the weekend that the operation might be postponed for several weeks to increase the president's chances of withstanding the surgery.
He had also held out the prospect in a television interview on Sunday that the operation might be cancelled altogther.
Yeltsin said earlier this month he had agreed to have an operation after doctors said the alternative was to adopt a "passive" way of life.
Yeltsin ducked out of public view shortly before he was re-elected on July 3 and Akchurin said at the weekend that the president had probably had a third heart attack around that time.
